field_sources.cli.version: B0 `grok --version` prints `grok 1.0.41 (4220f3b224a6) [alpha]` (re-verified 2026-09-23 against the 1.0.41 binary's strings: ImageGenInput 2 fields, ImageEditInput 3, ImageToVideoInput 4, ReferenceToVideoInput 9, VideoKeyframeInput 2, every limit string unchanged from 1.0.34; first verified on 1.0.13).
field_sources.model.image: D4 x.ai/news/grok-imagine-image-2 and the docs.x.ai release notes: `grok-imagine-image-2.0` GA since 2026-08-07; `grok-imagine-image-quality` (still the 1.0.41 binary's compiled-in default) retires 2026-11-02 — docs.x.ai/developers/migration/imagine-image-quality-nov-2: 'served by `grok-imagine-image-2.0` with `quality` set to `low`'. B8 1.0.34 documents `features.image_gen_model_override` ('Empty defers to the remotely configured default') and `features.image_edit_model_override`; one Imagine image model serves both tools, so grok-image writes this id into BOTH overrides before every launch and the manifest is what the CLI sends on a generation and on an edit alike. A deliberate pin: the remote settings (`settings_cache.json`, 1.0.41, 2026-09-23) carry both overrides as null, so an empty key runs the compiled-in, retiring `grok-imagine-image-quality`; the CLI lists no Imagine models and the C2PA `softwareAgent` says only `Grok Imagine`, so a newer Imagine id reaches this field only from the vendor's release notes.
field_sources.api_only: D4 Image 2.0 adds quality low|medium|auto, 1K/2K resolutions, background removal with transparent output; B1/B2 in 1.0.41 ImageGenInput is still {prompt, aspect_ratio} and ImageEditInput {prompt, image, aspect_ratio}, so none of these reach the CLI. D5 docs.x.ai/developers/release-notes (August 2026): 'Generation and editing support new formats including `21:9` (cinematic widescreen) and `5:2` (wide banners)' — neither is in the 1.0.41 aspect_ratio descriptions; stored-file inputs `image_file_id`/`video_file_id`/`reference_image_file_ids` are REST fields the tools do not carry. D6 docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/video/generation: `1080p` for text-to-video and image-to-video, and text-to-video itself; the 1.0.41 video tools take 480p|720p and a source image. Multi-reference edits (up to 5 on the API) and smart resize ride the existing `image` and `aspect_ratio` fields.
field_sources.model.video: B4 `grok-imagine-video-1.5`, adjacent to video_gen/mod.rs in the binary; the same id in the vendor reference-to-video documentation. No `video_gen_model_override` knob exists, so this one is pinned by the CLI version.
field_sources.refs.max: D2 docs.x.ai release notes: 'Image editing now accepts up to 5 source images per request (was 3)'. Live 2026-09-23 on 1.0.41 (`rawilimo`, session 01a0ced0-512c-7b21-9053-0365b2a82346): one image_edit call carried all 5 refs in `image` and returned 1280x720 with all five subjects — hence 5 with verified_max true. On 1.0.13 (2026-09-11) 4 refs got a text answer and no image_edit call. B2 the `image` schema states no cap; 5 is the endpoint's.
field_sources.aspects.generate: B1 ImageGenInput.aspect_ratio: "Aspect ratio of the generated image... Defaults to 'auto'. 1:1 for square (icons, profiles), 16:9 for wide (landscapes, cinematic), 9:16 for tall (phone wallpapers, stories), 3:2 for horizontal photos, 2:3 for vertical (portraits, posters)."
field_sources.aspects.edit: B2 ImageEditInput.aspect_ratio: 'Supported values: 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 3:2, 2:3, 2:1, 1:2, 19.5:9, 9:19.5, 20:9, 9:20, auto.' The same string records that single-image edits ignore the parameter and keep the source ratio.
field_sources.exact_size: B1/B2 ImageGenInput has 2 fields and ImageEditInput 3; neither carries a resolution, size, or quality parameter. The Imagine REST API has them (D3), the CLI tools do not.
field_sources.transparent: B2 no alpha/background parameter on either tool; B5 the image client writes `jpg`. Alpha comes from share/image-chroma.sh keying a green plate.
field_sources.resume: B6 `-r/--resume <SESSION_ID_OR_TITLE>`; D1 headless documentation resumes by the `sessionId` reported on the terminal event.
field_sources.video.tools: B3 image_to_video 'Generate a video from a single source image'; reference_to_video 'Generate a video from reference images and/or preset voices, guided by a required text prompt'.
field_sources.video.refs_max: B3 reference_to_video.images: 'Reference images, up to 14 entries' in 1.0.34 and 1.0.41 (7 in 1.0.13); the runtime error '`images` must contain at most N image references.' guards it.
field_sources.video.keyframes_max: B3 1.0.41 reference_to_video: 'set `first_frame` and/or `last_frame` (those images appear literally as the video's first/last frame; set both to interpolate, or the same image for a perfect loop) and/or `keyframes` (up to 4 `{image, timestamp_s}` anchors strictly inside the clip, snapped to a 1/3-second grid)'; runtime errors '`keyframes` must contain at most N anchors' and '`keyframes` timestamp s must be strictly inside the clip (0 < t < s)'; 'the index space follows the upload order `first_frame`, `images`, `keyframes`, `last_frame`'. grok-video wires all three as --first-frame, --last-frame, --keyframe <path>@<seconds>.
field_sources.video.voices_max: B3 reference_to_video.voices: 'up to 3 entries'; runtime error '`voices` must contain at most N preset voices.'
field_sources.video.voices: B3 the roster is not enumerated by the CLI: 'each a voice identifier from the built-in roster (e.g. "ara", "eve", "leo", "rex"; same voices as the xAI text-to-speech API; an unknown identifier fails with the list of available voices)'. null because no complete list is available offline; the four examples are the schema's own.
field_sources.video.durations: B3 image_to_video.duration: 'either 6 or 10 seconds. Default to 6 unless the user requests longer.'; runtime error '`duration` must be either 6 or 10 seconds.'
field_sources.video.reference_duration: B3 reference_to_video.duration: 'Duration of the video in seconds, between 1 and 15. Defaults to 6.'; B7 the bundled Imagine Video guidance repeats '`reference_to_video` accepts 1-15s'.
field_sources.video.resolutions: B3 both video tools: 'either 480p or 720p. Defaults to 480p'.
field_sources.video.aspects: B3 reference_to_video.aspect_ratio: '1:1 for square (icons, profiles), 16:9 for wide (landscapes, cinematic), 9:16 for tall (phone wallpapers, stories), 4:3 or 3:2 for horizontal photos, 3:4 or 2:3 for vertical (portraits, posters).' image_to_video has no aspect field at all (ImageToVideoInput has 4 elements: image, prompt, duration, resolution_name).
field_sources.video.container: B3 both tool descriptions point at `videos/1.mp4`; B5 the download client sends `video/mp4`.
field_sources.video.session_folder: B3 saved under the session's `videos/` folder, the video twin of `images/`.
field_sources.unsupported: B1/B2 no n/count ('To produce multiple images, emit multiple tool calls with distinct prompts'), no resolution, quality, seed, mask, response_format, or per-call model on either image tool; B3 image_to_video takes no aspect_ratio; B7 'Video starts from an image - there is no text-to-video tool.' D3 shows the REST API does expose n, resolution and quality, so their absence is a CLI limit rather than a model one.
